ind_rationale: Paper appraises evidence on patient safety benefits but does not substantiate the specific claim that immunological advantages provide indirect patient protection; likely a background/passing citation.
Paper supports higher postmenopausal CV risk in hyperandrogenic PCOS phenotype, but does not directly compare classical vs non-classical phenotypes as the claim asserts.
Paper shows kefir improves infected wound healing, but does not attribute effect to polysaccharides or innate immune stimulation as claimed.
Paper supports 5-HT3-dependent vagal signaling from luminal factors, but studies carbohydrates/osmolarity not lipids, involves no CCK1 mechanism, satiety, or human food-intake data.
Paper concerns obesity and female reproduction, with only general mention of obesity-induced inflammation; it does not substantiate leptin causing immune disorders in obese individuals.
Paper shows HDL decreased (not increased) with treatment, and TG/LDL reductions were non-significant, opposite to the claim of increased HDL.
